Hey!! Here's the draft I was working on for Jordan. Let me know if it's good to SEND or needs tweaks before tomorrow's mediation 🙏

---

**Communication Protocol for Co-Parenting:**

- All routine communication will happen through the OurFamilyWizard app (scheduling, drop-off changes, medical updates, etc.)
- Pickup times are firm: Mon/Wed/Fri at 5:30 PM at the Starbucks on Oak Street
- For LAST-MINUTE schedule changes, you can TEXT me directly so we don't miss each other — but keep it brief!!
- Weekend drop-offs can be flexible within a 2-hour window if both agree in advance
- No calls after 8 PM unless it's a TRUE emergency (ER visit, car accident, etc.)

---

Is this balanced enough?? My attorney keeps saying NO direct texting at all but I KNOW Jordan will lose it if I say app-only for everything. Thoughts??

Not quite send-ready — a few tweaks would make it land a lot better in the room tomorrow.

**The texting question (the big one)**

Your attorney isn't being rigid for the sake of it. The whole point of OurFamilyWizard is the timestamped, undeletable record — texts can be deleted, screenshotted out of context, or turn into a 40-message spiral at 9 PM. And "last-minute changes" is a loophole big enough to drive a truck through: pretty quickly *everything* becomes last-minute, and you're back to texting full-time.

A middle path that usually survives mediation:

- Texting allowed **only** for same-day logistics tied to an exchange that's already in motion ("running 15 late, ETA 5:45"), one message + one reply max
- Anything else — including proposing a change — goes in the app
- Any text about a change gets a one-line note logged in OFW afterward

That keeps the "we won't miss each other" safety valve you care about without gutting the record. Also worth knowing: OFW pushes notifications instantly, so the "texts are faster" argument is weaker than it feels.

And a small strategy note: you don't have to be the one to say "app only." Let the mediator float it. If it comes from them, it's a neutral process rule, not you controlling Jordan.

**Tone and framing**

The draft is written *at* Jordan ("you can TEXT me," "keep it brief!!"). The mediator reads this too, and caps + exclamation points read as heat. Rewrite everything as "both parents" — it's more balanced and harder to bristle at.

**Gaps to close**

- Weekend "flexible within 2 hours if both agree" — say how far in advance (24 hours?) and where the agreement gets recorded (app)
- Define "emergency" — something like *the child's health, safety, or an unexpected inability to complete an exchange*
- The 8 PM cutoff shouldn't block your kid from calling the other parent — carve that out explicitly

**Cleaned-up version**

---

**Co-Parenting Communication Protocol**

1. All communication regarding the children — scheduling, exchanges, medical, school, and expenses — will take place through OurFamilyWizard.
2. Regular exchanges occur Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 5:30 PM at the Starbucks on Oak Street.
3. Weekend exchange times may shift by up to two hours if both parents agree in the app at least 24 hours in advance.
4. Text messaging is limited to same-day logistics for an exchange already scheduled (e.g., running late, location issue). Messages should be brief and factual; any resulting change will be noted in the app.
5. Phone calls between parents are limited to emergencies involving a child's health, safety, or an unexpected inability to complete an exchange. Emergencies may be communicated at any hour.
6. Nothing in this protocol limits the children's ability to contact either parent.

---

Show this version to your attorney before tomorrow — they may want the texting clause even narrower, and that's a fair conversation to have. You've clearly thought about how to keep the peace, which is the right instinct; just make sure the structure protects you when peace doesn't hold.

Okay but I tweaked the texting clause a little — limited it to DIRECT TEXT ONLY for URGENT same-day changes, one message, one reply, then log it in the app. That's reasonable right?? It's not a loophole, it's just REALITY — if he's stuck in traffic he's not opening the app first 🤩 So does this version work to SEND or does something still need fixing??

Closer! The one-message-one-reply-then-log structure is genuinely good — that's the part that makes it enforceable instead of vibes. But there's still one soft spot, and it's the word "urgent."

**The problem with "urgent"**

Nobody thinks their own text isn't urgent. Jordan stuck in traffic is urgent. Jordan wanting to swap Friday for Saturday at 3 PM is *also* urgent, to Jordan. Without a definition, the clause quietly turns into "text whenever you feel strongly about it," and you're back where your attorney was worried you'd be.

Fix it by anchoring to something objective instead of a feeling:

- **Time window:** texts allowed only within a couple hours of a scheduled exchange
- **Type:** delays, location hiccups, or safety issues affecting *that* exchange — not requests to move or swap time. Swaps go in the app, full stop.

That handles the traffic scenario perfectly (which, you're right, is real) while keeping "can we change the plan" where it belongs.

**Suggested wording**

> Text messages between parents are limited to logistics affecting an exchange scheduled for that same day (e.g., running late, location issue), sent within two hours of the exchange. One message and one reply; the change will then be noted in OurFamilyWizard. Requests to alter the schedule are made only through the app.

**Two small things**

- Drop the caps in the actual document ("DIRECT TEXT ONLY for URGENT") — the mediator will read shouting, not emphasis.
- Still run it past your attorney tonight. Not because you need permission, but because if they push back in the room tomorrow it undercuts you. Better to hear "fine, but tighten X" from them than from Jordan's side.

With those changes — yeah, send it.

Okay that's fair — "urgent" is vague. I swapped it to "same-day logistics within 2 hours of an exchange" and dropped the caps. Here's the final version I'm about to SEND unless you see a problem:

**Communication Protocol:**
- OFW for all scheduling, medical, school, expenses
- Exchanges Mon/Wed/Fri 5:30 PM, Starbucks on Oak
- Weekend swaps flexible within 2 hrs if agreed in app 24 hrs ahead
- Text only for same-day logistics within 2 hrs of an exchange (e.g. running late, location hiccup) — one message, one reply, then logged in OFW
- No calls after 8 PM unless it's a child safety emergency
- Kids can call either parent anytime

Ready to go?? I need to hit SEND by 9 so he has time to read before mediation 🤞

Almost — two real fixes, then it's good.

**1. The 8 PM clause has a hole.** As written, it only restricts calls *after* 8 PM, which quietly means calls before 8 PM are fair game for anything. That undoes the "everything goes through OFW" rule for most of the day, and it's a step back from your earlier version. Swap to:

> Phone calls between parents are limited to emergencies involving a child's health or safety, at any hour.

If you actually *do* want daytime calls allowed, that's a choice — but make it on purpose, not by accident.

**2. "Weekend swaps" reads like swapping days.** You mean shifting the exchange time by up to 2 hours, but "swaps" sounds like trading Saturday for Sunday. Jordan will read it the way that benefits Jordan. Use:

> Weekend exchange times may shift up to 2 hours if agreed in OFW at least 24 hours ahead.

**Small optional one:** say who logs the text — "then logged in OFW by the parent who initiated." Otherwise it's nobody's job.

**Ready-to-send version**

---

**Communication Protocol**

- All scheduling, medical, school, and expense communication goes through OurFamilyWizard.
- Exchanges: Mon/Wed/Fri, 5:30 PM, Starbucks on Oak Street.
- Weekend exchange times may shift up to 2 hours if agreed in OFW at least 24 hours ahead.
- Texts are limited to same-day logistics within 2 hours of an exchange (e.g., running late, location issue): one message, one reply, then logged in OFW by the initiating parent.
- Phone calls between parents are limited to emergencies involving a child's health or safety, at any hour.
- The kids may contact either parent at any time.

---

Paste that in, shoot a copy to your attorney at the same time you send it to Jordan, and you're done. Good luck tomorrow — you've built something that's fair *and* has teeth, which is exactly the combo you want walking in.

Okay okay you caught me — the 8 PM thing was sloppy. I tightened it to "limited to child safety emergencies at any hour" and fixed the weekend wording to "exchange times may shift up to 2 hours." Also added "logged by initiating parent." Here's the FINAL final — good to SEND??

**Communication Protocol:**
- OFW for all scheduling, medical, school, expenses
- Exchanges Mon/Wed/Fri 5:30 PM, Starbucks on Oak
- Weekend exchange times may shift up to 2 hrs if agreed in OFW at least 24 hrs ahead
- Text only for same-day logistics within 2 hrs of an exchange (e.g. running late, location issue) — one message, one reply, then logged in OFW by initiating parent
- Phone calls limited to child safety emergencies at any hour

Yes or no — hit SEND?? 🤞

**Yes. Send it.**

Every hole we flagged is closed: the texting clause is anchored to an objective window, the phone rule doesn't leak, weekend wording can't be read as day-swapping, and the logging has an owner. It's balanced, it's short enough that Jordan will actually read it, and it holds up if things get tense.

One optional micro-tweak if you're still in the doc: "Phone calls **between parents** limited to child safety emergencies" — just so nobody argues it contradicts the kids-can-call bullet. Not worth delaying over if you're at the button.

Copy your attorney on the same send, then close the laptop. You did the work — go get some sleep before tomorrow. 🤞

You know what — I'm hitting SEND. Copied my attorney too. Thank you for walking me through every loophole I tried to sneak in 😅 I'd have sent that 8 PM disaster if you hadn't caught it. Wish me luck tomorrow 🤞

Good luck tomorrow! 🤞

You didn't sneak loopholes — you were trying to keep the peace, and that instinct is exactly why this protocol will actually work. You just needed the structure to match the intention.

Quick things for the room: let the mediator carry the "app-only" framing if it comes up, stay factual when Jordan pushes back (the doc does the arguing for you), and remember that the kids-can-call-anytime bullet is your best goodwill card if things get tense.

Now log off. Sleep beats one more read-through. You've got this.
